newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan reports progress in Afghan peace shuttle.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan reports progress in Afghan peace shuttle.

text.p: Pakistan said on Thursday that its peace shuttle to war-torn neighbour Afghanistan had made "some progress" and would not be deterred by the new outbreak of fighting there.

A Foreign Ministry spokesman said a Pakistani emissary, who has been shuttling between the warring Afghan factions since last month, would again go to the opposition-held northern town of Mazar-i-Sharif within two to three days and would later go to Tehran to consult Iranian officials.

"Some progress has been made," he told reporters at a news briefing about previous trips to Afghanistan by a team led by senior Foreign Ministry official Iftikhar Murshed. "Both sides have stated that they want a peaceful settlement."

But amid the stepped peace efforts, fighting has intensified north of the capital of Kabul with the opposition forces making gains against the Taleban, which controls more than two-thirds of Afghanistan.

"The latest outbreak of fighting is unfortunate," the Pakistani spokesman said. "It will, however, have no impact on our determination to continue with the shuttle mission. We are determined to promote the intra-Afghan peace process."

He said the proposal to form a political commission, which was demanded by the opposition alliance to chart the outlines of a future broad-based government, had been discussed and was "emerging as a distinct possibility".
"Confidence-building measures are now required," he said.
The spokesman said Pakistani mediators had conveyed the Taleban movement government's demand for release of its officials detained in Mazar-i-Sharif since late May to the opposition alliance.
Pakistan says it wants to bring the protagonists "within negotiating range" and then to convene an intra-Afghan dialogue with the participation of countries bordering Afghanistan.
In addition, it wants the United States and Russia to be the guarantors of any peace accord.
The spokesman said Pakistan had completed its discussions with the countries bordering Afghanistan and "they will shortly be updated on the progress of the shuttle mission".
On a parallel track, he said, Pakistan was coordinating closely with Iran and a U.N. special mission on Afghanistan.

An Iranian deputy foreign minister, Alaeddin Boroujerdi, visited Islamabad on July 17, when Pakistani officials said the two sides agreed in talks to combine their moves to bring peace in Afghanistan.

Differences between Pakistan and Iran on the Afghan conflict widened after Islamabad recognised the Taleban government in May, while Iran has continued to recognise ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani.
